title: TimeSeries<T> with STL-compatible iterators
summary: A generic container of observations that plugs into the standard algorithms, then the classic analytics written with them: returns, moving averages, drawdown and volatility.

steps.title: A container with iterators
hints: Wrap a `std::vector<T>` and forward `begin()`/`end()` (const and non-const overloads).
Expose `using value_type = T;` and the iterator types: algorithms and range-for need them.
The iterator-pair constructor is itself a template: `template <typename It> TimeSeries(It first, It last)`.

steps.title: Returns and moving average
hints: `std::transform` with two input ranges: `(p.begin() + 1, p.end())` and `p.begin()`.
Moving average in O(n): keep a running sum, add the new value and subtract the one leaving the window.

steps.title: Drawdown and volatility
hints: Running peak with `std::partial_sum` and a max lambda, as in the chapter's exercise.
